newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek banks order their brokers to resume trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek banks order their brokers to resume trade.

text.p: Greek state banks ordered their subsidiary brokerages to resume trading on the Athens bourse on Tuesday after three days of upheaval which stopped all transactions due to the Delta Securities scandal, brokers said.

Floor traders of state brokerages of National, Ionian and Commercial banks were at their trading terminals at the exchange and Reuters screens showed bids and offers for shares but there was no trading.
Other member brokerages, attending an emergency meeting at their association's headquarters, expressed confusion and uncertainty over how to react to the state move to force open the bourse.
Brokers said that Alpha Brokerage, a subsidiary of private Alpha Credit Bank had also shown up but it had not been confirmed.
They also said that private Ergo Bank was under pressure to order its brokerage to resume trade.
Despite some thin bids and offers there was no sign of any trades being executed in the apparent battle between part of the brokerage community and the national economy ministry.
